title: Pixels to Tokens: Token Space Efficient Active Learning for Low-Budget Semantic Segmentation
abstract: arXiv:2610.20881v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: While foundation models and vision transformers (ViTs) have redefined visual representations, current active learning (AL) strategies for these backbones largely operate at the patch or region level, where annotation requirements remain high due to extensive pixel labeling. Extending ViT-based AL to the pixel-level, low-budget regime is uniquely challenging: with as little as one pixel query per image, a method must simultaneously identify the most informative locations and train a reliable decoder head from an extremely sparse signal. We introduce TEAL (Token-space Efficient Active Learning), the first pixel-level AL framework built around ViT representations. TEAL uses a frozen ViT backbone and performs diversity-based selection directly on its native token lattice, avoiding the artifacts introduced by interpolating token embeddings to dense pixel resolutions. translated_title: 从像素到词元：面向低预算语义分割的词元空间高效主动学习
translated_abstract: 尽管基础模型和视觉Transformer（ViT）已经重新定义了视觉表示，但目前针对这些骨干网络的主动学习（AL）策略大多在补丁或区域级别上运行，由于需要进行大量的像素标注，标注需求依然很高。将基于ViT的主动学习扩展到像素级、低预算的场景尤为困难：在每张图像仅查询一个像素的情况下，方法必须同时识别出最有信息量的位置，并从极其稀疏的信号中训练出可靠的解码器头。我们提出了TEAL（Token-space Efficient Active Learning，词元空间高效主动学习），这是首个围绕ViT表示构建的像素级主动学习框架。TEAL使用冻结的ViT骨干网络，并直接在其原生词元网格上执行基于多样性的选择，从而避免了将词元嵌入插值到密集像素分辨率时所引入的伪影。我们的框架在多层词元上应用了两级MaxHerding策略
tldr: 提出了首个基于ViT表示的像素级主动学习框架TEAL，通过在冻结ViT骨干的原生词元网格上直接执行两级MaxHerding多样性选择，实现了极低标注预算下高效的语义分割。
en_tdlr: TEAL, the first pixel-level active learning framework built on ViT representations, performs two-level MaxHerding diversity selection directly on the frozen backbone's native token lattice, enabling efficient semantic segmentation under extremely low annotation budgets.
